newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rebound on technicals, earnings.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rebound on technicals, earnings.

text.p: Mexican stocks had reversed an earlier slump and were modestly higher at midday Friday.
Traders said prices gained on a technical rebound and were also boosted by corporate earnings reports that were more favorable than those seen Thursday.
"It's partly technical: Prices had fallen sharply and then rebounded," one desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 13.53 points, or 0.36 percent, at 3,787.24.

"Earnings were a bit slack at first, but then last night we saw Telmex, which was in line with expectations, and Bancomer, which was good, which has improved things a little," another desk trader said.
Telecomms firm Telmex was up 12 centavos at 16.56 pesos, against an early low of 16.30 pesos. Bancomer, one of Mexico's largest financial groups, was up 17 centavos at 2.76 pesos.
"They sold Telmex early on speculation; earnings were not so bad at all," a trader said.
Telmex ADRs had also reversed an earlier slump and were up 1/4 at 42, bucking a downtrend on Wall Street. The Dow industrials were down 39.73 points at 6,752.52.
Traders said the bourse's revival could be short-lived.
"We don't quite believe what is happening," one trader said.

Overall trading volume was moderate at 44.1 million shares. Desk traders, however, said they were busier than usual because open outcry had been suspended on the stock exchange floor to be replaced for the day by screen trading.
